### Authorization (RBAC)
Two models coexist, gated by `session.ums_version`:
- **v1 (legacy)**: `routes/aclroutes.js:13-18` → `lucyACLcheck.acl_check()` (`routes/lums/acl.js`), backed by `models/ums_groups.js` and `models/routes_access.js` (per-access-level route allowlists).
- **v2 (current)**: `lib/helper/getUserRoles.js` resolves a user's roles (Redis-cached, falling back to `models/userProfile.js`), then `roleHasPermission(roles, module, action)` checks a static matrix in `middleware/rbac/rolesPermission.js`. Route-level enforcement is `hasPermission(module, action)` (`middleware/rbac/permissionMiddleware.js:69-123`), wired per mount-path by `routes/permissionWrappers.js`'s `registerRouteWithPermission()` using static `MODULE_PATHS`/`METHOD_TO_ACTION`/`CUSTOM_ACTIONS` tables.
- `middleware/rbac/userOperationMiddleware.js` adds a second layer for user-mutation endpoints (blocks self-modification, protects Admin/Superadmin accounts from lower roles).
- `middleware/ldapRoleRefresh.js` keeps LDAP-derived roles fresh in the background (non-blocking, Redis-TTL-gated).

---

## Important Business Logic

**1. Bot-to-human live agent hand-off.**
A chat message from an end-user, when a hand-off condition is met (`lib/scripts/liveAgentTransfer.shouldTransfer` or the desk/queue system), is registered against a "desk" (`agentTransfer.registerTransfer` → checks desk availability/queue limits via `QueueManager` and `models/agentAssist/{Desk,DeskSetting}`), broadcast to available agents over Socket.IO (`liveAgentv2.js` Broker events), and once an agent accepts, subsequent messages are relayed both ways (`publishToUser`/`publishToAgent`), with per-transfer state (language, inactivity timers) tracked in Redis (`TransferManager`) and active-chat sets per agent (`ActiveChatsManager`, Redis SADD/SREM for race-free updates).

**2. Multi-provider GenAI conversation turn.**
A conversation turn is normalized through `lib/corearchitecture.js`'s `CoreArchitecture.continueConversation()`, which enforces a recursion guard (max 5) and a trial-tenant message cap (500), then dispatches to `GLOBAL.Dispatcher.service(GLOBAL.Dispatcher.CGS, ...)` → the appropriate provider module (`openai.js`/`bedrock.js`/`vertex.js`/etc.) → optionally an agentic tool-calling loop (`cognitiveServices/openai/agents.js`) that can call any registered `tools/*` function or a configured external A2A agent.

**3. Multi-channel bot delivery.**
`connectorBots/index.js` builds and caches one Bot-Framework `CloudAdapter`-based connector per channel (Teams/Slack/Telegram/etc.), publishing a `GLOBAL.ConnectorBotTriggers` object that other modules (`agentTransfer`, `notifications`, `chatMessages`) call into to actually deliver messages/proactive notifications/meeting invites back out to the channel, regardless of which channel it is.

**4. Tenant provisioning.**
New tenants are bootstrapped (not "migrated" in the schema sense) by `migrate/core.js`/`migrate/manage.js`: creating an initial admin user, publishing default Map-Reduce views, seeding a default Super Admin access group, and populating the tenant's enabled admin-console catalog (`migrate/manage.js`'s hardcoded ~18-entry console list).

---

## Important APIs

| Method | Endpoint | Purpose | Main handler | Important downstream logic |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `POST` | `/` (login) | Authenticate a user (LUMS/LDAP/OAuth/none, tenant-dependent) | `routes/index.js` (`POST /`) + `routes/lums2.js`/`routes/lums/ldapLogin.js` | Sets `req.session.*`, writes `models/userlogin.js` audit record |
| `GET` | `/user_info` | Return current session's user info, permissions, CSRF token | `routes/naclroutes.js` | `getUserRoles`/`calculateUserPermissions` (`lib/helper/getUserRoles.js`) |
| `GET` | `/admin` | Serve the admin console SPA | `routes/admin.js` | Reads built `dist/index.html` (prod) or proxies to Vite dev server |
| `GET` | `/agents` | Serve the live-agent console SPA | `routes/naclroutes.js` | Reads built `dist/agent.html` (prod) or proxies to Vite dev server |
| `GET` | `/admin/agentassist/desk/:title` | Fetch a live-agent desk's details | `routes/liveAgentConsole/desks/index.js` | `models/agentAssist/desk.js` via Dispatcher |
| `PATCH` | `/admin/agentassist/desk/:title` | Update a desk + settings | `routes/liveAgentConsole/desks/index.js` | Updates model + resets Redis queue counters via `QueueManager` |
| `GET` | `/notify/fetchNotifications` | Fetch an agent's push notifications | `routes/pushNotification.js` | `models/pushNotification.js` |
| `POST` | `/genAI/playground` | One-off LLM prompt/response for the GenAI playground UI | `routes/genAI/index.js` | `lib/scripts/gptPrompter.prompt()` |
| `POST` | `/genAI/nlp_to_code` | Natural-language-to-code helper | `routes/genAI/index.js` | `lib/scripts/gptPrompter.prompt()` |
| (CRUD) | `/genAI/agents/*` | Manage GenAI agent definitions (create/version/import/export) | `routes/genAI/agents/index.js` | `models/genAIAgents`, `genAIAgentVersions`, `genAIAgentChangelog`; validates tools via `tools/index.js` |
| `GET`/`POST` | `/oidc_login`, `/oidc_authenticate/:authenticator_id`, `/oidc_callback` | Tenant-configurable OIDC SSO flow | `routes/index.js` | `models/oidcAuthenticator.js`, `lib/helper/utilities.js` |
| `POST` | `/auth/sso/callback` | SAML/AppID SSO callback | `routes/federation/index.js` | `passport.authenticate('saml'/AppID strategy)` |
| `POST` | `/chatbot/msteams/login` | MS Teams tab SSO | `routes/index.js` | `lib/helper/msteamsAuth.js` |

*(This table covers representative, verified endpoints — `routes/` contains ~40 feature areas; see [Recommended Reading Order](#recommended-reading-order) for how to explore the rest.)*

---

## Data Flow

1. **Inbound chat message** → Socket.IO (`lib/socket/chat.js`) or channel webhook (`connectorBots`) → `CoreArchitecture.continueConversation()` → GenAI dispatcher → (optionally) tool calls / A2A calls → response streamed back over the same channel.
2. **Tenant configuration** → stored as documents in the primary DB (Mongo/Cloudant/DynamoDB, per tenant's `service_keys`) → read through `lib/helper/caching.js`'s 1-hour Redis cache → consumed by nearly every request (`customer_credentials` in session).
3. **Live-agent transfer state** → written directly to Redis (queue counters, active-chat sets, per-transfer metadata) for low-latency real-time coordination, with the durable transfer/conversation record persisted via `models/agentAssist/*` (Dispatcher-backed).
4. **User roles/permissions** → computed once from LDAP groups or UMS group membership, cached in Redis with a TTL, refreshed in the background (`ldapRoleRefresh`), and re-derived into a permission map served to the frontend via `/user_info`.
5. **Built frontend assets** → `vite build` → `dist/` → `buildEngine/uiCacher.js` Brotli-compresses and uploads to object storage/CDN (`config.cosui.bucketpath`) → served to browsers from the CDN, with only `dist/index.html`/`dist/agent.html` read from local disk by the Express app.

---

## Dependencies

Selected dependencies from `package.json` and why they're used:

| Dependency | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `express`, `express-session`, `express-handlebars` | Core web server, sessions, server-rendered views |
| `socket.io`, `@socket.io/redis-adapter` | Real-time chat/live-agent/workflow-monitor events, horizontally scaled via Redis pub/sub |
| `redis`, `@redis/client`, `@redis/entraid`, `connect-redis` | Redis client (standalone/cluster), Azure Entra ID Redis auth, session store |
| `mongodb`, `@ibm-cloud/cloudant`, `@aws-sdk/client-dynamodb` | Pluggable primary database backends |
| `passport`, `@node-saml/passport-saml`, `ibmcloud-appid`, `jsonwebtoken`, `jose` | Authentication (local, SAML, AppID/OIDC, JWT handling) |
| `ldapts` | LDAP directory connectivity |
| `bcrypt`, `speakeasy`, `password-validator` | Password hashing, MFA/TOTP, password policy |
| `botbuilder`, `botframework-connector` | Microsoft Bot Framework channel integrations |
| `@a2a-js/sdk` | Agent-to-Agent protocol client/server |
| `@aws-sdk/*`, `@azure/*`, `ibm-cos-sdk`, `@ibm-functions/iam-token-manager` | Cloud provider SDKs for secrets, object storage, compute, cost, email (SES) |
| `twilio` | Voice/IVR and SMS channel integration |
| `web-push` | Browser push notifications (PWA) |
| `lusca`, `nocache`, `helmet`-like headers via `lusca` | Security headers (CSP, HSTS, nosniff) |
| `joi` | Input validation |
| `vue`, `vue-router`, `pinia`, `vite`, `@vitejs/plugin-vue` | Frontend SPA framework and build tooling |
| `vitest`, `@vue/test-utils`, `supertest`, `sinon`, `proxyquire` | Testing |
| `module-alias` | `@lib`/`@models`/etc. import aliasing |
| `husky` | Git hooks (pre-commit lint/test, commit-msg format check) |
| `exceljs`, `pdf-parse`, `mammoth`, `tesseract.js` | Document/OCR processing (likely for knowledge-base ingestion) |
| `markdown-it`, `slackify-markdown`, `slackify-html` | Markdown rendering / Slack Block Kit conversion |
| `geoip-country`, `mobile-detect` | Request context enrichment |

---

## Testing

- **Framework**: Vitest (`vitest.config.js`), not Jest — though the mocking/assertion API (`vi.mock`, `expect(...).toHaveBeenCalledWith(...)`) is Jest-compatible.
- **Config** (`vitest.config.js`): aliases mirror `package.json`'s `_moduleAliases`; `include: ['tests/**/*.test.js']`; coverage over `lib/`, `routes/`, `models/`, `middleware/` (text/html/lcov/cobertura reporters, **no enforced thresholds**); `setupFiles: ['./tests/setupAliases.js', './tests/setupTests.js']`.
- **Global test mocks** (`tests/setupTests.js`): fakes `global.GLOBAL.Dispatcher` (callback-style DB mock) and `global.config`; `global.redisClient` is mocked **per test file** as needed (e.g. `tests/routes/pushNotification.test.js:32-34`).
- **`tests/setupAliases.js`**: patches Node's `Module._resolveFilename` so `require('@lib/...')` resolves under Vitest too, and stubs `@a2a-js/sdk` with a local fixture (`tests/stubs/@a2a-js/sdk`).
- **Structure**: mirrors the source tree — `tests/routes/` (largest, ~111 files), `tests/lib/` (~64), `tests/models/` (~10), `tests/middleware/` (~4).
- **House pattern** (e.g. `tests/routes/pushNotification.test.js`): dynamically `import()` a route module, reach into the Express router's internal `.stack` to grab the exact handler function, and invoke it directly with mock `req`/`res` — bypassing HTTP/supertest for route unit tests.
- **How to run**: `npx vitest` (or `npx vitest run` for a single pass). **Note**: `npm test` / `npm run testcommit` do **not** run Vitest — they run `tests.js`, a small gate script that checks the Node version (`code` arg) or validates a commit message format (`commit` arg, enforced by `.husky/commit-msg`).
- **Linting** runs via `npm run lint` → `.husky/linter` → ESLint over `.vue,.js,.jsx,.cjs,.mjs`, with a few legacy files excluded.

---

## Build and Run

```bash
# Install dependencies
npm install

# Configure the project
# Set AEX_ENV (aks|eks|onprem) and NODE_ENV, plus the secret-store variables
# for your chosen AEX_ENV (see Configuration section). For pure local/dev,
# leave AEX_ENV unset and NODE_ENV != 'production' — dev.js supplies a
# hardcoded subdomain and a local, unauthenticated Redis client is used.

# Run the backend locally (Express + Socket.IO)
npm start                 # node app.js — needs Node 24.x

# Run the frontend dev server (Vite, serves src/ and src-agent/)
npm run serve             # vite, default port
npm run client            # vite --host 0.0.0.0 --port 3001 (bash-only NODE_OPTIONS syntax —
                           # on Windows/PowerShell, set NODE_OPTIONS separately first)

# Run tests
npx vitest                # actual unit test run
npm test                  # only checks Node version (does NOT run vitest)

# Lint
npm run lint

# Build frontend for production
npm run build              # vite build (writes dist/)
                            # postbuild runs automatically: buildEngine/uiCacher.js
                            # (compresses + uploads dist/ to object storage/CDN)
npm run bundle              # legacy chat-widget bundle under public/

# Start in production mode
NODE_ENV=production npm start   # or via Docker: docker build -t aex-web . && docker run -p 8080:8080 aex-web
```

---

## Developer Guide

| Task | Where to look |
|---|---|
| **Add a new API** | Pick the right router tier (`routes/unauthroutes.js` public, `routes/naclroutes.js` logged-in, `routes/aclroutes.js` admin/RBAC) and add a route file under the matching `routes/<feature>/` folder. If it needs RBAC v2, register it via `routes/permissionWrappers.js`'s `registerRouteWithPermission()` and add a module/action entry to `middleware/rbac/rolesPermission.js`. |
| **Change business logic** | Business logic lives in `lib/scripts/<module>/`, not in route files — route handlers should stay thin and delegate. Find the relevant module in [Core Modules](#core-modules) first. |
| **Add a new integration** (external API/service) | If it's an LLM/agent tool, add a new folder under `tools/` following `tools/example.tools.js`'s shape and register it in `tools/index.js`. If it's a new GenAI provider, add a module under `lib/scripts/dispatchers/cognitiveServices/openai/` and wire it into `gptCaller.js`. If it's a new DB backend, add it to `lib/scripts/dispatchers/dbServices/index.js`'s `services` map. |
| **Change configuration** | `lib/helper/envConfiguration.js` — find the right `AEX_ENV` branch. Remember `IS_REDIS_CLUSTER_MODE` is currently only wired for `aks`/`eks` (see [Unknowns](#unknowns--areas-requiring-further-investigation)). |
| **Fix an API bug** | Trace the router chain (`unauthroutes.js`/`naclroutes.js`/`aclroutes.js`) to find where the route is mounted, then the feature folder under `routes/`. Check `middleware/rbac/` if it's a permissions issue, or `lib/helper/getUserRoles.js` if it's a roles/permissions-computation issue. |
| **Add tests** | Mirror the source path under `tests/` (e.g. `routes/foo/index.js` → `tests/routes/foo/index.test.js`). Reuse `tests/setupTests.js`'s `GLOBAL`/`config` mocks; mock `global.redisClient` per-file as needed. Follow the "grab the handler off the router's `.stack`" pattern from `tests/routes/pushNotification.test.js` for route-level tests. |

---

## Code Flow Examples

**1. A tenant admin views a live-agent desk (`GET /admin/agentassist/desk/:title`)**
`app.js:243` (mount `aclroutes.js`) → `aclroutes.js:62` (`csrfLoginCheck` + mount `admin.js`) → `admin.js:85` (`adminLogger` audit) → `admin.js:113` (`registerRouteWithPermission` inserts `hasPermission('agentAssist','view')`) → `liveAgentConsole/index.js:11` → `desks/index.js:18` (`isUserAdmin` role check) → `new Desk(req.session).get(title)` (Dispatcher-backed model) → `res.json({deskDetails})`.

**2. An end user's chat message triggers a live-agent hand-off**
Browser Socket.IO client (`socket.io-client`, no `query.agent`) connects → `lib/socket/chat.js`'s single `io.on('connection', ...)` registers end-user listeners (`send message`, etc.) → message handling checks `lib/scripts/liveAgentTransfer.shouldTransfer` (or the newer desk system via `agentTransfer.registerTransfer`) → if transferring, `QueueManager`/`models/agentAssist/Desk` check availability → an available agent's socket (connected with `query.agent=true`, routed through `liveAgentv2.js`'s `'Transfer Broker'` events) receives the transfer → `TransferManager`/`ActiveChatsManager` track state in Redis → subsequent messages relay via `agentTransfer.publishToUser`/`publishToAgent`.

**3. A GenAI agent calls an external tool (e.g. Slack) mid-conversation**
`CoreArchitecture.continueConversation()` (`lib/corearchitecture.js`) → `GLOBAL.Dispatcher.service(GLOBAL.Dispatcher.CGS, ...)` → provider module (e.g. `openai.js` for Azure OpenAI) → `cognitiveServices/openai/agents.js`'s agentic loop presents the agent's configured tool functions (looked up via `tools/index.js`'s `getAllToolFunctions()`) to the LLM → on a function call, `agents.js` executes `TOOLS[toolName].function(toolArgs)` (e.g. `tools/slack/index.js`'s exported function, using the tenant's stored `SLACK_BOT_TOKEN`) → result is fed back into the conversation and a final response streamed to the user.

---

## Key Things To Understand

1. **`GLOBAL`, `config`, `redisClient`, and `passport` are bare global variables**, not imports/DI — set once at startup and relied on everywhere (declared in `.eslintrc.cjs:13-20` as ESLint globals). New code should follow this convention rather than trying to "fix" it into a DI pattern mid-feature.
2. **`GLOBAL.Dispatcher` is the single point of indirection** for databases, GenAI providers, object storage, and third-party services — never instantiate a Mongo/Cloudant client directly; go through `GLOBAL.Dispatcher.service(...)`.
3. **The default database backend is Cloudant, not MongoDB** — `DB_TYPE` must be explicitly set to `mongodb` (or `dynamodb`) to change it.
4. **Route authorization is layered, not single-gate**: the coarse `unauthroutes → naclroutes → aclroutes` split, the legacy v1 ACL system, and the v2 RBAC permission matrix all coexist depending on `session.ums_version`.
5. **There is no centralized error-handling middleware** — every route formats its own error response, inconsistently. Don't assume a shared error shape.
6. **Redis is critical infrastructure**, not optional caching — sessions, Socket.IO scaling, and live-agent state all depend on it being up.
7. **Two independent Vue SPAs** (`src/` at `/admin`, `src-agent/` at `/agents`) are built from **two separate Vite entry points** and are otherwise unrelated codebases sharing conventions — don't assume a change in one affects the other.
8. **`migrate/` is tenant provisioning, not schema migration** — don't look here for a versioned-migrations framework.
9. **`agentTransfer` (desk/queue system) and `liveAgentTransfer` (rule-based bridge) are two separate, coexisting live-chat hand-off mechanisms** — check which one a given channel/feature actually uses before changing either.
10. **The "tool" plugin shape is a strict contract** (`{name, fields, functions[]}`) consumed by the GenAI agentic loop — new tools must follow `tools/example.tools.js` exactly to be invocable by an LLM.
11. **Models are not a single pattern** — check whether a given model extends `BaseModel`, is a legacy standalone prototype, or is pure-Redis before assuming its behavior.
12. **`npm test` does not run the unit test suite** — it only checks the Node version. Use `npx vitest` directly.
13. **Frontend build output is expected to be served from a CDN**, not the app server, in production (`vite.config.js`'s `base` + `buildEngine/uiCacher.js`'s upload step) — only the top-level `index.html`/`agent.html` are read from local disk by Express.
14. **Socket.IO runs entirely on the default namespace/path**, multiplexed by query params (`query.agent`, `query.scheduler`, `query.workflowMonitor`) rather than separate namespaces.
15. **`IS_REDIS_CLUSTER_MODE` is only wired for `aks`/`eks`** — setting the env var alone does nothing for `onprem` today (a known gap, not yet fixed as of this README).

---

## Recommended Reading Order

1. `package.json` — scripts, dependencies, module aliases.
2. `app.js` — the entire startup/wiring sequence (read top to bottom).
3. `lib/helper/envConfiguration.js` — configuration and secrets per environment; how `redisClient` is created.
4. `lib/corearchitecture.js` — the base conversation-handling class and the `GLOBAL.Dispatcher` pattern in action.
5. `lib/scripts/dispatchers/index.js` and `lib/scripts/dispatchers/dbServices/index.js` — the DB abstraction.
6. `models/base/index.js` + one concrete model (e.g. `models/channel.js`) — how models use the Dispatcher.
7. `routes/unauthroutes.js` → `routes/naclroutes.js` → `routes/aclroutes.js` — the routing/auth tiers, in that order.
8. `middleware/rbac/permissionMiddleware.js` + `routes/permissionWrappers.js` — RBAC v2.
9. `lib/socket/chat.js` → `lib/socket/liveAgentv2.js` — the real-time layer.
10. `lib/scripts/agentTransfer/index.js` — the live-agent hand-off orchestrator.
11. `lib/scripts/dispatchers/cognitiveServices/index.js` → `openai/gptCaller.js` → `openai/agents.js` — the GenAI/LLM layer and tool-calling loop.
12. `tools/example.tools.js` — the tool plugin contract.
13. `src/main.js` + `src/routes/index.js`, then `src-agent/main.js` + `src-agent/routes/index.js` — the two frontend SPAs.
14. `tests/setupTests.js` + one representative test (`tests/routes/pushNotification.test.js`) — testing conventions.
15. `DevOps/README.md` — CI/CD pipelines.

---

## Unknowns / Areas Requiring Further Investigation

- **`config/config.js`** is referenced by `lib/helper/envConfiguration.js:177` as the local/dev default config, but **does not exist in this checkout**. Local development without `ENV_DEFAULT_CONFIG` set would throw. It's likely a gitignored/developer-supplied file — not confirmed.
- **`npm run worker` → `node jobs/index.js`** (`package.json:17`): no `jobs/` directory exists anywhere in this repo. Either a stale/aspirational script or the folder is generated/external — not confirmed.
- **`config-back.js`** (repo root): references Cloudant/Memcache/LDAP/"Dialog Service" credentials that don't match any current `AEX_ENV` branch. Appears to be a legacy leftover; not confirmed whether anything still requires it.
- **`lib/scripts/dispatchers/dbServices/cosmosHandler/`** exists on disk but is not registered in the DB backend-selection map (`dbServices/index.js:1-5`) — likely dead/unwired code; intent not confirmed.
- **`lib/scripts/entityDetection/index.js`** — no code anywhere in the repo appears to `require` it; likely orphaned, not confirmed.
- **`IS_REDIS_CLUSTER_MODE`** is set in the `aks` and `eks` config branches (`envConfiguration.js:58,163`) but **not** in the `onprem` branch (`:65-114`) — so an on-prem deployment cannot currently enable Redis Cluster mode by env var alone without a small code change. (See earlier discussion in this conversation for the exact fix.)
- **Two Redis-unsafe patterns** exist that would need fixing before relying on Redis Cluster mode in practice: `routes/lums/ldap.js`'s `terminateTenantSessions()` (single-cursor `SCAN` + multi-key `DEL`, not cluster-slot-safe) and `tools/redis/src/{setKey,getKey,deleteKey,listKeys}.js` (open their own standalone connection, bypassing the shared cluster-aware client).
- **`lib/loginhandler.js` / `lib/ldapHandler.js`**: only reachable via `routes/end_point_auth.js`, which is commented out in both route tiers — treat as legacy/dormant, not confirmed fully dead.
- **Exact `PORT` value in the root/onprem/dev Dockerfiles**: none of them set `ENV PORT`, so `process.env.PORT` (used directly in `app.js`'s production `listen` call) must be injected by the orchestrator — the exact value used in each deployment topology wasn't confirmed beyond `deployment/ibm/Dockerfile` (`ENV PORT=8080`) and the on-prem nginx config's proxy target (`http://aex-app:3000`).
- **`lib/helper/ToolHandler.js`** and its exact runtime role alongside `tools/index.js`'s `getToolDescription`/`getAllToolFunctions` was referenced but not fully read — worth a closer look if working on the tools/agent-configuration UI.
- **`lib/scripts/gptPrompter/promptAdvisor/` and `enhanceMessageAdvisor/`** consumers were inferred by naming convention, not confirmed by an exact call-site read.
- **A2A `callMCP.js` (Model Context Protocol) exact configuration path** was not investigated in depth.
- **`package-lock.json` is gitignored** (per `.gitignore`) — dependency versions are not pinned via lockfile in this repo; reason not documented anywhere found.

labels.name: new-feature
labels.description: Wholly new functionality (for release notes categorization)

type.name: Feature
type.description: A request, idea, or new functionality

items.body:
### Description

Serve branding to unauthenticated clients so the login page can render the customer's identity before anyone signs in.

No endpoint serves operator-configured application data anonymously today: `AuthHelper.PERMITTED_ENDPOINTS` covers only `/v?/health/**` and `/v?/connector/register`, with `OAUTH2_ENDPOINTS` covering the login flow. This is the first anonymous endpoint to expose customer content, so the response shape is deliberately narrow.

Scope:

- `BrandingControllerImpl` implementing `GET /v1/branding`, read-only, returning `PublicBrandingDto`.
- Register the path in `AuthHelper.PERMITTED_ENDPOINTS`.
- The response is built by explicit field mapping from the branding settings; it never returns a settings DTO directly, so a future settings field cannot leak by inheritance.
- Reads go through the existing `SettingsCache`, so the anonymous path adds no database load per request.

Anonymous disclosure of the customer's logo and brand colours is an accepted, stated trade-off recorded in the Epic.

### User Story

As an anonymous visitor, I want the instance to show its owner's identity on the login screen, so that I can tell I am on the right system before entering credentials.

### Use Case

An unauthenticated browser requests `GET /v1/branding` and receives the configured colours, logos and default theme, and nothing else.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. [ ] `GET /v1/branding` returns branding without authentication and is registered in the permit-all list.
2. [ ] The endpoint is read-only; any other HTTP method against it is refused.
3. [ ] The response type contains branding fields only and is populated by explicit mapping, not by returning or extending a settings DTO.
4. [ ] A test asserts the serialized anonymous response contains exactly the expected branding keys, and fails if any additional settings field appears.
5. [ ] The endpoint reads through `SettingsCache` and issues no per-request database query.
6. [ ] With branding unset, the endpoint returns platform defaults rather than an error.
7. [ ] Existing authenticated settings endpoints and the OAuth2 login flow are unaffected; their tests pass unchanged.
8. [ ] Sonar quality gate passes and new code meets at least 80% coverage.

> **Re-target — [`DECISIONS.md` `D-16`](../docs/DECISIONS.md) (2026-10-22).** **VOID:** `P5-12` (#67, NDR + COD), `P5-15` (#81, cores + warranty holds). **Partially VOID** (each header names the void part): `P5-08` (#48, trade-customer persona), `P5-09` (#52, channels + tracking links; cross-dock stands), `P5-11` (#62, rate quotes, serviceability, AWB pools; tracking events and status mappings stand), `P5-13` (#72, OEM obsolescence + marketplace claims; grading stands), `P5-23` (#123, the `OBSOLESCENCE` claim type). The dealer/services adapter modules in this epic's header are removed. The channel-order exit clause is withdrawn.

Part of #1 · Modules `warehouse-3pl` (new) · `warehouse` · `warehouse-adapter-dealer` · `warehouse-adapter-services` · Migrations — **four blocks, enumerated below** · Ships in **v2**

## Overview

**23 tasks. Three products sharing one base, and two of them can be built in parallel by two teams.**
Round 4 filed five more P5 task files under `D-14` item 7 and, on 2026-09-10, folded each into its most
similar existing task (no duplicate tasks; `#157`–`#161` closed as duplicates): the trade-customer
portal into `P5-08` as its second persona, the print-template scopes into `P5-21`, and the rest into v1
hosts as **v2 increments built in this wave** — the v2 junctions into their parent-table owners
(`P0-04`, `P0-06`, `P0-11`, `P1-01`, `P1-02`, `P1-03`, `P1-05`, `P1-14`, `P2-04`), inter-company sale
and purchase into `P1-17`, value-banded approval levels into `P2-23`, registry translations into `P1-19`.

- **3PL** — clients as objects with contracts and onboarding templates, charge codes, versioned
  effective-dated rate cards, **the append-only reversible billable-event meter**, storage billing in four
  methods with the minimum-monthly true-up as a *visible metered event*, billing runs with a frozen
  approved state, accessorials, disputes, the AR handover envelope, freight billing modes, SLA
  definitions and measurements and breaches, the client portal as a **permission surface**, and row-level
  owner segregation **with a negative test per endpoint**.
- **Channels and carriers** — channel accounts and idempotent order import, publish rules as the oversell
  control, tracking events normalised **and** raw, rate shopping with the quote persisted, pincode
  serviceability, AWB pools claimed transactionally, NDR with a response clock, COD remittance
  reconciliation, RTO as an inbound stock stream.
- **Reverse logistics** — grading at receipt, obsolescence returns, the marketplace claim window, recall,
  cores, warranty scrap-and-hold, NRV write-down as a register, the COGS recognition policy.

**The whole phase stands on concessions already made in v1**, and none of them can be made now:
`owner_id NOT NULL` in the position key (`D-5`), `whb_lpns.received_at`, **outbox events at billable
granularity** (`PC-42`), `cost_basis` including `ZERO_BAILMENT`, owner-scoped access grants, and the
persisted daily storage snapshot whose start date is `PNR-3`. R4 §5.3 puts it plainly: `warehouse-3pl` is
*"a thin module standing on a wide base concession, and the concession is not optional, not deferrable
and not flaggable."*

## The invariants this phase establishes

This phase **establishes no new `L-n`** — `P0` and `P1` did that. What it does is put existing
invariants under **new writers**, and a new writer is exactly how an invariant is lost. Each row names
the invariant, the new writer, and the specific way this phase could break it (`H-008`).

| # | Invariant | The new writer P5 introduces | How this phase breaks it if unwatched |
|---|---|---|---|
| **L-14** | **Non-own stock is never valued.** `owner_type != OWN` hands over for quantity and custody only | **3PL billing** — the first subsystem whose whole purpose is to attach money to somebody else's stock | this is the invariant P5 is most likely to break, and it would look like a feature. Billing prices a **service** (storage, handling, accessorials) against a client, and posts to AR through `wh3_ar_handovers`. It never writes a valuation row against `owner_type != OWN`, and no billing run may be the reason a stock value appears |
| **L-10** | **Allocation is an open-item ledger** | **channel/marketplace order intake** and the returns-grading path | a marketplace connector that "reserves 40" against a channel rather than against a holder quad reintroduces the counter the invariant exists to forbid. Every channel reservation carries the same quad as a demand-order reservation |
| **L-11** | **Ownership never changes silently** | **returns grading, refurbishment and RTO/NDR**, where goods change hands as a side effect of a workflow | a graded unit that becomes ours, or a client's unsold stock that becomes ours at contract end, is an explicit title-transfer movement type with its own reason code — never an `UPDATE` of `owner_id` |

## Exit criterion — as scenario ids

**`WH-SC-234`** is **half the v2 exit criterion** (the other half, `WH-SC-239`/`WH-SC-240`, is `P4`'s):
*a 3PL bills a client for a month of storage and handling from metered events.*

`IMPLEMENTATION-PLAN.md` §1.7 adds **three clauses that make it a real test**, and all three are in this
phase's acceptance:

1. **The invoice arithmetic is reproducible from the meter** — re-rating the same period against the same
   card version returns the same total (`P5-03`, `WH-SC-234` · `WH-SC-236`).
2. **A client user in the portal cannot see another client's stock through any endpoint**, proved by a
   **negative test per endpoint** (`FR-300`; `P5-08`, `WH-SC-140` · `WH-SC-244`).
3. **A channel order imported twice on the same `(channel account, external order id)` produces one
   demand order** (`P5-09`).

The full walked set for the phase: **`WH-SC-032` · `WH-SC-135` · `WH-SC-137` · `WH-SC-140` ·
`WH-SC-200` · `WH-SC-233` · `WH-SC-234` · `WH-SC-235` · `WH-SC-236` · `WH-SC-237` · `WH-SC-238` ·
`WH-SC-244` · `WH-SC-296`** — **thirteen**, plus the scenarios thirteen tasks must author (below).

## ⚠ Twenty of this phase's requirements have no scenario, and that is a gate, not a footnote


`SCENARIO-CATALOGUE.md` §4.2 lists them honestly: of 71 unproven requirements, **43 are v2**, and the bulk
of those are this phase's — the whole carrier/channel surface (`FR-198`, `FR-200`–`FR-204`, `FR-208`–`FR-210`),
returns (`FR-272`, `FR-276`–`FR-279`), 3PL (`FR-293`, `FR-295`, `FR-297`, `FR-298`, `FR-303`), valuation
(`FR-241`, `FR-243`), replenishment (`FR-254`, `FR-259`), execution (`FR-223`, `FR-226`, `FR-227`),
`FR-140`, `FR-181`, `FR-267`, `FR-338`, `FR-343`, `FR-445`.

`IMPLEMENTATION-PLAN.md` §10 requires that *"the `WH-SC-nnn` scenarios the task claims to close are
**walked in the running app**"* — so a task with none has nothing to walk. **Seventeen P5 tasks therefore
author their own scenarios as their first act** (`P5-05`, `P5-06`, `P5-07`, `P5-09`, `P5-10`, `P5-11`,
`P5-12`, `P5-13`, `P5-15`, `P5-16`, `P5-17`, `P5-18`, `P5-19`, `P5-20`, `P5-21`, `P5-22`, `P5-23`).
Round-2 correction (`H-007`): the word said *thirteen* while the list held fifteen ids, and the two
round-2 task files were missing from both. `P5-22` and `P5-23` are the sharper case — their
`## Scenarios closed` sections hold **unnumbered prose bullets** rather than no scenarios at all
(*"a key is issued, the plaintext is shown once, and a second read returns only `hasValue`"*;
*"a GRN short by four units raises a claim from the receipt screen, pre-filled from the receipt line"*).
Those bullets are real scenarios that were never allocated ids: the first act of each task is to
number them from the `WH-SC-306` marker and add the rows to `SCENARIO-CATALOGUE.md`, not to invent
new prose. `P5-14` is correctly absent — it closes catalogued scenarios only.

> **⚠ ID COLLISION IS THE OBVIOUS FAILURE.** New ids continue from **`WH-SC-306`**
> (`SCENARIO-CATALOGUE.md` §5 rule 3), and two parallel P5 tasks will both take 301.
> **The rule for this phase: claim your ids by merging them into `SCENARIO-CATALOGUE.md` in one commit
> BEFORE writing code.** The catalogue file is the allocation register; nothing else is.


## `A-3` — P5 builds screens over tables that already exist

`H-008` found that this epic cited none of the four ladder amendments, and that the one it most needs
reaches no phase epic at all. **`A-3` (`DECISIONS.md` §5.1) put the item-variant *schema* in v1 and
kept only the *screens* in v2** — so `P5-20`'s Style × Variant Matrix (`WS-033`) and `WS-032`'s Variant
Axes & Values are built **over `V500014`/`V500015`, which `P1-01` already shipped**. The failure this
paragraph exists to prevent is a P5 lead reading their own epic, finding no variant model, and
authoring a second one. `whb_items.style_item_id` and the axis/value tables are the model; the only
genuinely missing table in this area is `FR-445`'s ratio/assortment **pack template**, which is
`P5-20`'s own new table (`V500064`) and is recorded three sections down.

## Migration blocks — re-derived from the task headers, not transcribed

```bash
# from issues/ — the header line of every P5 task file
grep -h '^Part of' p5-*.md | sed 's/.*Migrations //; s/ · Screens.*//'
grep -h '^Part of' p5-*.md | grep -oE 'V5[0-9]{5}' | sort -u
```

| Band | Module | Numbers this phase claims | Owners |
|---|---|---|---|
| `V510000`–`V519999` | `warehouse` | `V510200`–`V510214` **+ `V510215`, `V510216`** · round 4: **`V510221`**, **`V510223`**, **`V511209` + `V511239`** | `P5-09` `V510200` `V510208` `V510209` · `P5-10` `V510201`–`V510202` · `P5-11` `V510203`–`V510205` · `P5-12` `V510206`–`V510207` · `P5-13` `V510210` **+ `V510215`** · `P5-14` `V510211` · `P5-16` `V510212` · `P5-17` `V510213`–`V510214` · **`P5-23` `V510216`** · **`P5-08` `V510221` + the pair `V511209`/`V511239`** (the trade persona, folded from former `P5-25`) · **`P5-21` `V510223`** (print-template scopes, folded from former `P5-24`). `V510221` and `V510223` are carved from the correction reserve and the pair is `WH-206`'s (`IMPLEMENTATION-PLAN.md` §2.9 rows 2a and 7). Round 4's other app claims left this phase at the fold: `V510220` is `P1-14`'s, and `V510222`, `V511180` and `V511210`/`V511240` are `P2-23`'s — v2 increments of v1 tasks, built in this wave |

| `V530000`–`V539999` | `warehouse-3pl` | `V530000` · `V530010`–`V530011` · `V530020`–`V530021` · `V530030`–`V530031` · `V530040`–`V530044` · `V530050` · `V531000`–`V531099` | `P5-01` … `P5-07` |
| `V500064`–`V500199` | `warehouse-base` post-v1 DDL | `V500064` · `V500065` · **`V500066`** | `P5-20` ratio-pack templates · `P5-21` packaging balances · **`P5-22` API clients and keys** (`WHB-67`, not `WHB-66` — see `DATA-MODEL.md` §7), plus `whb_api_client_endpoints` and `whb_api_client_companies` (`RG-018`). The two numbers this row once called *"still to claim"* were claimed in round 1; the third is round 2's. Round 4's base numbers `V500069`–`V500077` are claimed by P0/P1 hosts as v1.1 or v2 increments since the 2026-09-10 fold, so no P5 header carries them |

**Not this phase's, and it is easy to assume otherwise:** **`V530060` (`W3-13`,
`wh3_client_gst_registrations`) belongs to `P4-10`** — a P4 task inside the 3PL band, because the band
follows the table's prefix and the task follows the requirement's phase (`IMPLEMENTATION-PLAN.md` §2.9
divergence 6). `P4-10` therefore depends on `P5-01`, and it is **the only P4→P5 dependency in the plan**.

**Exactly one task owns each number.** A task needing a second file takes the next number **inside its own
block**, never the next globally free one.

## Build order

`IMPLEMENTATION-PLAN.md` §3.8 graphs this phase; this is the same information as a schedule. **`A → B`
means A precedes B.**

- **First task: `P5-01`** — the module scaffold, the client object and the build-time ratchet. Every
  other P5 task and one P4 task (`P4-10`) hang off `wh3_clients`.
- **Long pole: the billing chain, `P5-02 → P5-03 → P5-04 → P5-05`.** `P5-05` is where the money
  freezes, and `P5-03` is where it is measured — an event vocabulary that cannot price per line cannot
  be repaired downstream.
- **⚠ The one edge drawn across four phases: `P0-11 → P5-03`.** `P5-03`'s **first act** is to verify
  `P0-11`'s event vocabulary. If `pick.line.confirmed` does not carry quantity, item and location, then
  per-line handling billing — how every audited 3PL prices — is **permanently unavailable for the
  past**, the defect is `P0-11`'s, and this phase stops until it is fixed.
- **Parallel streams**, once `P5-01` lands: `{P5-02 → P5-03 → P5-04 → P5-05}` billing · `{P5-06}` and
  `{P5-07}` freight and SLA, both joining at `P5-05` · `{P5-22 → P5-09 → P5-10, P5-11, P5-12}` the
  integration surface then channels, match, carriers and NDR/COD · `{P5-13, P5-14, P5-15}` reverse
  logistics · `{P5-16, P5-17}` NRV and weighing/labour · `{P5-18, P5-19, P5-20, P5-21, P5-23}`.
- **`P5-08` (the portal) is scheduled after `P5-05`, not beside it.** It is a permission surface over
  screens that must already exist, and the thing it exposes to a client is the billing run.
- **Round 4's P5 work is increments of existing tasks, not tasks** (folded 2026-09-10). The trade-customer
  persona is built inside `P5-08`, after its client persona; the print-template scopes inside `P5-21`.
  The v2 increments of v1 hosts (`P0-04`, `P0-06`, `P0-11`, `P1-01`, `P1-02`, `P1-03`, `P1-05`, `P1-14`,
  `P1-17`, `P1-19`, `P2-04`, `P2-23`) are scheduled into this wave's gaps. Schedule `P1-03`'s v2 increment
  before `P5-18` where possible: the site-scoped supplier preference is what sister-branch replenishment
  reads per site (`WH-SC-324`).

## Tasks


**Sizing** (`IMPLEMENTATION-PLAN.md` §9.3): 1 XL · 6 L · 15 M · 6 S. **Staffing** (§9.4): 3–4 backend,
3 frontend, 1 mobile, 2 QA. *"Two independent sub-streams. Billing needs someone who has built billing
before."* §9.5 assumption 6: **P4 and P5 are two products** — they run fully concurrently with two teams
and one shared base reviewer, and cannot be compressed into one team without serialising v2.

## Four defects found in `IMPLEMENTATION-PLAN.md` §2.7 while authoring this phase

All four are recorded in `DEFECTS-FOUND.md` and fixed in the task files rather than carried silently.

1. **`FR-279` (the marketplace return-claim window) has no table and no screen.** `V510210` creates only
   the three grading/obsolescence tables (`DATA-MODEL.md` `WH-110`); `wh_return_receipts.claim_due_at`
   carries the clock alone; and all 237 screen ids in `BUILD-SPEC-SCREENS.md` §1 are claimed and none is
   this. **`P5-13` claims `V510215`** from §7.3's correction reserve and allocates a new screen id.
2. **`FR-445` (the ratio/assortment pack template) has no table.** The variant *axes* exist (`V500014`)
   and `whb_items.style_item_id` exists — the **pack template naming a quantity per variant** does not.
   **`P5-20` claims a number in §7.2's declared `V500064`–`V500199` post-v1 base gap.**
3. **`FR-343` (returnable packaging's per-counterparty balance) has no table**, and `G-024` marks it as
   *new* relative to `F-060`, which covers packaging as stock only. **`P5-21` claims a number in the same
   base gap.**
4. **`P5-01`'s `V531000`–`V531099` sub-allocates `W3-20`'s declared `V531000`–`V531199`**, and §2.9 —
   which enumerates every other sub-allocation and asserts *"Six"* — does not record it.

## Traps this phase must not get wrong

- **Every verb in a §4 Actions cell is a `@PreAuthorize`, not an `:edit`** (`H-001`). The strings are
  rows in `BUILD-SPEC-SCREENS.md` §10.2 — twenty-five were added in round 2 and are seeded by `P5-01`
  (`V531000`–`V531099`) — and **a screen whose verbs §3/§7 describes only in prose must enumerate them
  in the task before the controller is written.** The failure this prevents is already visible in the
  document: `wh3_billing_runs:approve` existed while `:cancel` did not, so anyone who could edit a
  draft run could cancel an invoiced one.

- **⚠ The meter's granularity reaches back into base and cannot be fixed here.** `PC-42`/`F-012`: *"a
  design that emits only `order.shipped` makes per-line handling billing — how every audited 3PL prices —
  permanently unavailable for the past."* **`P5-03`'s first act is to verify `P0-11`'s event vocabulary**;
  if `pick.line.confirmed` does not carry quantity, item and location, the defect is `P0-11`'s and this
  phase stops until it is fixed.
- **⚠ There is no outbox precedent anywhere in this repository.** `grep -rli "outbox"` → **0 files**
  (`PC-35`). If `P0-11` budgeted *"a table"*, the missing five items — gapless cursor, publisher job,
  retry with backoff, dead-letter grid, replay-from-cursor — surface in `P5-03`. `@Async` is not a
  substitute; `reference_async_notification_lazyinit` is a live trap in this repo.
- **⚠ `PNR-3` decides what is billable at all.** Storage billing, ageing, days-on-hand and obsolescence
  *"all begin on the day the [snapshot] job was switched on"*. A period before it **cannot be billed by
  any method**, and `P5-04` must refuse rather than return zero.
- **⚠ Owner segregation has four leak sites per grid, not one** — grid, **export**, **statistics map**,
  dropdown (`WH-SC-242`), plus the availability API and the lineage query. A `403`, **never an empty
  grid** (`WH-SC-140`): an empty grid reads as *"no stock"*, not as a boundary.
- **`warehouse-3pl` contains no invoice, no numbering sequence and no tax engine, in any version.**
  Asserted by the coupling test: *"a `wh3_` invoice table appearing in any migration fails the module's own
  coupling test"* (`WH-SC-238`).
- **Non-own stock is never valued** (`L-14`). *A 3PL that posts its clients' stock to its own balance
  sheet has a catastrophe in both directions.* The custody number is a **different number on a different
  report**, and the assertion is *the number is absent*, not *zero*.
- **`FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED` has zero precedent in this codebase** (R1 `C-040`). `P5-11`'s AWB pool and
  `P3-02`'s task claiming both need it — write and review it **once**.
- **Five objects in this phase will move to `logistics` in P6** (R7 §2.6): `wh_carriers` /
  `wh_carrier_services` / `wh_carrier_accounts`, `wh_shipment_tracking_events`, `wh_shipment_ndrs`,
  `wh_cod_remittances` — and `wh_rto_consignments` **never fully**, because the receipt stays.
  **All five are referenced by stable string code resolved through a service, never by an FK from the
  referencing table into the relocatable one.** *"Applying that rule to one object and not the other four
  is how the move stops being cheap"* (`G-013`).
- **The ratchet is "zero commits to `warehouse-base`", never "zero commits to `platform`"** (`D-10`
  corollary, `G-047`). This phase adds ~25 grids; every one edits `filterUtils.ts` (213 scopes, a missing
  field is **silently dropped**) and `CacheConfiguration.java` (234 names, an unregistered name throws on
  the **first call**, not at startup). Budget the merge contention (§9.5 assumption 2).
- **Filter-aware statistics get no cache name at all** — `CacheConfiguration.java:190-196` records that
  exact mistake (classic#790, #791; R1 `C-043`).
- **The table is `filter_definitions`** (`platform/…/V229:8`); **`grid_filter_definitions` does not exist**
  and inserting into it crash-loops the backend (R1 `CM-4`). `grid_preferences` needs **both**
  `default_columns` and `default_filters`.
- **Every warehouse frontend filename must be globally unique** — `Dockerfile.frontend:80-177` merges
  module `src/` last-write-wins (R1 `C-012`).

## Blocked on decisions

- **⛔ `OD-3`** blocks **`P5-01`** — *"before `warehouse-3pl` starts"*. One database per customer;
  a 3PL's clients are an **owner dimension, not tenants**. `grep -ril "tenant" platform/backend/src/main/java`
  → **0 files**. **Do not re-litigate.**
- **⛔ `OD-1`** reaches **`P5-16`** — the reciprocal accounting edits that let warehouse own cost while
  accounting owns the ledger (`D-6`). It is *a different repository's design set to amend*.
- **`OD-5`** (does the frontend re-close the vocabularies the backend opens) lands first in this phase at
  `P5-02`'s charge-code categories and `P5-13`'s condition grades.
- **`OD-9`** is already answered — **warehouse never computes tax** — and `P5-05` depends on it.
- **⛔ `OD-18`** blocks **`P5-09`'s drop-ship requirement `FR-467`** (round 4, `RK-005`) — *what v1
  records for a drop-shipment*, answered by the first drop-shipped purchase. The channel work in `P5-09`
  proceeds; the drop-ship movement type is **not** seeded in v1, and any module seeds it under `D-10` once
  the row is answered.

## Definition of done
Per #1 — including the four additions specific to this programme, of which two bite hardest here:
**every `L-n` invariant has a database guard *and* a service guard, and the service guard rejects first
with a field-level error**; and **every threshold column ships with the scheduled job that reads it**
(`P5-07`'s SLA windows, `P5-11`'s AWB low watermark, `P5-12`'s NDR clock and COD ageing, `P5-13`'s three
windows, `P5-15`'s two, `P5-17`'s certificate expiry). *A dated obligation with no actor is a defect at
the moment it is merged.*

items.title: perf(iotdb rest): health check runs `show databases` on every tick
items.body:
## Summary

The IoTDB connector (REST driver mode) runs `show databases` on every health-check tick via the auth-check path, in addition to the TCP-level `check_ping_restapi`. Returns one row per IoTDB storage group (a.k.a. database).

## Where

`apps/emqx_bridge_iotdb/src/emqx_bridge_iotdb_connector.erl:521-…` (`check_auth_restapi/2`).

```erlang
%% pseudo:
POST /rest/v2/nonQuery  body={"sql":"show databases"}
```

Note: this is only the REST driver. The thrift driver uses `iotdb:ping(Conn)` which is bounded.

## Impact

The row count is operator-controlled (one per storage group / database), not customer-data-proportional, so cost stays small in practice. But:

* The list scales linearly with the number of storage groups the IoT deployment partitions data into. Deployments with many sites / regions can have hundreds.
* It runs on every health-check tick in addition to the cheaper TCP-level ping that already exists.

## Suggested fix

Two options, in preference order:

1. Replace `show databases` with `SELECT 1` via the same REST endpoint. Bounded to a single-row response regardless of storage-group count.
2. Rely on `check_ping_restapi` alone for liveness and move the auth check into startup only. Auth credentials don't drift at runtime; re-checking them on every health tick is the wrong cadence.

## Related

Part of the health-check audit following d94cbde4. YELLOW (bounded but more expensive than necessary).

## Summary

The Full Import that follows an export dies with an unhandled `InvalidOperationException` when a Connected System Object it is updating holds two attribute values for its External ID attribute. `ConnectedSystemObject.ExternalIdAttributeValue` uses `SingleOrDefault`, which throws on a duplicate; nothing between it and the run catches that, so `SafeFailActivityAsync` fails the whole Activity. Nothing on the Activity says which object, and every object still to be processed is abandoned.

Both halves matter. The duplicate is a defect. Failing the run outright rather than reporting the object through a Run Profile Execution Item is a second one, and it is the sort CLAUDE.md's synchronisation integrity rules exist to forbid: all errors reported via RPEIs, never silent, never a raw exception out of the run.

## Observed

Scenario 16 (JIM SQL Connector matrix), the confirming Full Import on an accounts Connected System after an Export. Twelve identical failures across one run, six per provider, on both Microsoft SQL Server and Oracle:

```
[21:56:50 ERR] SafeFailActivityAsync: Unhandled exception whilst executing sync run for activity 01a00c93-...
System.InvalidOperationException: Sequence contains more than one matching element
   at System.Linq.ThrowHelper.ThrowMoreThanOneMatchException()
   at JIM.Models.Staging.ConnectedSystemObject.get_ExternalIdAttributeValue() in ConnectedSystemObject.cs:line 180
   at ConnectedSystemServer.ProcessConnectedSystemObjectAttributeValueChanges(...) in ConnectedSystemServer.cs:line 4870
   at ConnectedSystemServer.LinkUpdateChangeRecords(...) in ConnectedSystemServer.cs:line 4704
   at SyncServer.UpdateConnectedSystemObjectsAsync(...) in SyncServer.cs:line 264
   at SyncImportTaskProcessor.PerformImportAsync() in SyncImportTaskProcessor.cs:line 796
```

The database holds exactly one External ID value per Connected System Object, so the duplicate is transient and in memory, on the update path.

## Consequence

The confirming import never completes, so nothing exported is ever confirmed, so the next synchronisation stages another Create for the same person, so the next Export inserts a second row. Observed: 78 rows in `APP_USERS` for 39 distinct people, every one duplicated, and JIM's own Connected System Object count for that Object Type climbing past the population on each cycle. A defect in a read-only property therefore duplicates rows in the customer's target database, one more per synchronisation cycle, until somebody notices.

## Where it happens

`ProcessConnectedSystemObjectAttributeValueChanges` applies `PendingAttributeValueAdditions` to the CSO's `AttributeValues`, then applies `PendingAttributeValueRemovals`, then (when change tracking is on) reads `ExternalIdAttributeValue` to record `DeletedObjectExternalId` on the change. If the anchor's old value has been queued for removal and its new (identical) value queued for addition, both are present in `AttributeValues` between the add and the successful remove; if the removal does not match, both stay, and the read throws.

The removal matches by `Id` when the pending removal carries one, and by reference when it does not (`Guid.Empty`). A removal whose persisted `Id` is not the `Id` of the instance in the loaded collection removes nothing. That is the most likely mechanism, but it is not yet pinned; see the open question.

## Proposed fix

Two changes, and neither is optional.

1. **Report, never throw, out of the update path.** Whatever the read finds, an object with two External ID values is a per-object error naming the object and the two values, raised as a Run Profile Execution Item, and the run continues. `ExternalIdAttributeValue` is a model property and can stay strict; the caller on the import path is what must not let it out.
2. **Fix the duplicate itself.** Establish why the removal fails to match (see below), and make the add-then-remove sequence unable to leave two values behind. A regression test that puts a CSO through an update whose anchor value is replaced by an equal value, with change tracking on, and asserts one External ID value afterwards.

## Open question for whoever picks this up

Which two values collide, and why the removal misses. Reproduce with Scenario 16 on `fix/duplicate-pending-export-guard-stack-scenario16` (any export row) and inspect the CSO's `AttributeValues` at the point of the throw: same value or different, and whether the pending removal's `Id` matches any instance in the collection. That answers whether this is an `Id`-mismatch on the removal, or two genuinely different anchor values, which would point somewhere else entirely.

## Found by

The Scenario 16 matrix under the three-Connected-System topology (#170). It is the only thing now standing between that matrix and a near-clean run.

items.title: Add asyncio locks to CustomerRegistry for concurrent access safety
items.body:
## Issue Description

The `CustomerRegistry` cache currently doesn't handle concurrent access safely, which could lead to race conditions in multi-threaded environments where multiple coroutines check cache expiration simultaneously.

## Related

- PR #4 Claude Review - Medium Priority Issue #3
- Originally identified during Phase 3 MCP connector implementation

## Current Behavior

```python
if customer_id in self._cache:
    cached = self._cache[customer_id]
    if datetime.now() < cached.expires_at:
        return cached.config
    else:
        del self._cache[customer_id]  # Race condition here
```

Multiple coroutines could:
1. Both check expiration simultaneously
2. Both decide cache is expired
3. Both delete and query database
4. Duplicate database queries occur

## Proposed Solution

Use `asyncio.Lock` per customer_id:

```python
from asyncio import Lock
from collections import defaultdict

class CustomerRegistry:
    def __init__(self, ...):
        self._cache: OrderedDict[str, CachedConfig] = OrderedDict()
        self._locks: defaultdict[str, Lock] = defaultdict(Lock)
    
    async def get_customer_config(self, customer_id: str) -> Optional[CustomerConfig]:
        async with self._locks[customer_id]:
            # Check cache
            if customer_id in self._cache:
                cached = self._cache[customer_id]
                if datetime.now() < cached.expires_at:
                    return cached.config
                del self._cache[customer_id]
            
            # Query database (unchanged)
            ...
```

## Impact

**Breaking Change**: This requires making `get_customer_config()` async, which will require updates to all callers.

## Priority

Medium - Important for production deployments with concurrent access patterns, but current implementation works for single-threaded/low-concurrency scenarios.

## Files Affected

- `src/paidsearchnav_mcp/clients/bigquery/customer_registry.py`
- All callers of `get_customer_config()` (will need to be updated to use `await`)

items.title: The case for multitenancy
items.body:
<!-- Before you post an issue or if you are unsure about something join our matrix channel https://app.element.io/#/room/#opsdroid-general:matrix.org and ask away! We are more than happy to help you. -->
# Description
This is meant to be more of a good spirited discussion than an "issue". Please consider it as such.

Let's say you create an opsdroid with a certain set of skills, and now you would like multiple groups/organizations/customers/whatever to use these skills. It feels like currently the way to do this would be to set up an opsdroid _PER_ group/organization/customer/whatever. I say this because of the configuration file. Each `connector` in this file is able to have 1 token or credential set or whatever in that file.

What I would like to propose/brainstorm is a way that we could achieve multitenancy with opsdroid so that we can install one opsdroid instance and then use that to respond to requests from multiple organizations using the same skills. I am actively working on a POC for this using the Github connector (because that is my current use case) but I fear this is a short-sighted approach and that if the group thinks multitenancy could be an interesting thing, then it should be more on a full opsdroid level.

Anyways, just wanted to open this topic for discussion.

## Declaration

I want to admit that I am likely the "corporate shill" here, and I understand that I may be advocating for things that more corporate users of opsdroid would like rather than a typical use case. But I'm also attempting to get my company to be a supporter of OSS in general, and I'm using much of my experience with this project as the launchpad. However, I would like to be respectful of this project's intentions while I advocate for new things. So I'm hoping that taking both viewpoints into consideration is possible. Thank you.

items.body:
After updating from Npgsql 3.2.7 to 4.0.0 (Update from .net core 2.0 to 2.1.1 as well) i have located a new Problem.

In some rare cases (high concurrency and unittests) i get this Error from `NpgsqlConnection.ReloadTypes()` (stack below)

The project setup is a multi tenant application using postgres schema to separate tenant data and structure, in test case 1 db with 2 schema. both schema have the same structure (types and tables) but can be different (optional).
I'm using postgres enum types and Npgsql ConnectionPool is active.

normaly i could use `GlobalTypeMapper` to map enums but i have connections to a separated log database as well, in this case registred enums will cause a error similar to "not existing type in database" (at least in 3.x versions) i can't remember the exact wording.

My workaround was to use `connection.TypeMapper.MapEnum` for each connection after open, this was working fine in 3.x even switching between schema by `SET search_path =` was no problem, no need vor type reload.

i need to switch schema by command not via connectionstring parameter because i want to use a common pool of connections for all tenants, i have hundreds of tenants and separted pools would use to much postgres connections for this reason i can't change this.

After updating to 4.0.0 the following changed: my first connection was on schema A and after getting the connection next time from the connection pool i want to use it for schema B the connection.TypeMapper.MapEnum` throws an exception `A PostgreSQL type with the name schema_name.enum_type_name was not found in the database`. After some debugging i noticed the need of loading DB types for each schema in every connection. For this I'm using ReloadTypes on every not initialized connection per schema (i know, its realy bad for performance, but however).
this reload logic is surrounded by lock, something like this:

``` C#
lock (TypesLoaded)
{
	if (!TypesLoaded.Contains(checkKey))
	{
		TypesLoaded.Add(checkKey);
		connection.ReloadTypes();
	}
}
```
`checkKey` is Host+ DBName + SchemaName + connection.ProcessID
